admission.capacityNote: 250 places a year, filled by a two-round selective admission and reviewed on a rolling basis from 1 October 2026. Not numerus fixus: the deadlines are UCM's own, 1 February 2027 for non-EU/EEA applicants and 1 April 2027 for EU/EEA and Swiss applicants.

selection.description: First round: the Board of Admissions reviews your application documents and decides whether to interview you.
Second round: an online interview in English with a UCM academic staff member, 30 to 45 minutes, on your academic plans and how UCM would support them. The decision follows within six weeks.

requirements.label: A full IB Diploma

officialWording.text: To qualify for admission to a bachelor's programme at Maastricht University (UM), you must hold a secondary school diploma that is considered equivalent to the Dutch pre-university VWO diploma.

requirements.note: Nuffic compares the full IB Diploma to a VWO diploma. Maastricht warns separately that being VWO-equivalent does not by itself satisfy a programme's additional subject requirements, which are assessed on their own. On Course Results specifically, Maastricht says nothing at all: its diploma list names the "International Baccalaureate Diploma, at least 3 Higher Level (HL) subjects" and no page on the site mentions DP Course Results, an IB Certificate or a partial IB. That silence is not permission — the requirement is a diploma, and Nuffic compares Course Results to vwo-deelcertificaten, which are not one.
requirements.alternativeRoute: This programme's own admission page publishes no route, and that absence was checked rather than assumed: it states the requirement as a VWO diploma, an HBO or OU propaedeutic diploma, or a non-Dutch diploma equivalent to VWO, and the word colloquium appears on it only in the site menu. Maastricht does run Colloquium Doctum admissions under article 7.29 of the Dutch Higher Education Act — its Faculty of Law publishes one for 2027-2028 at 100 euro, written on 12 May 2027 and oral on 26 May 2027, open to applicants who are at least 21 at the start of the academic year and requiring the English rather than the Dutch language requirement; its Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences publishes another; and University College Venlo publishes one on the same kind of page that University College Maastricht leaves blank. So the question for this programme is not whether the university can do it but whether this faculty will, and the only way to find out is to ask its admissions office in writing, early, naming article 7.29 WHW. Two doors are shut whatever the answer: Maastricht "does not accept Foundation Programmes for admission to a bachelor's programme", and it "does not accept equivalency statements", so a Nuffic credential evaluation will not stand in for the diploma. And all of it waits for your 21st birthday. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the only route that reaches this at eighteen. One further route is national rather than this institution's, and it is the only one that produces the qualification itself instead of an exemption from it: the Dutch staatsexamen vwo. Anyone who registers may sit vwo subjects one at a time with DUO — registration for the 2027 examinations runs from 15 October to 31 December 2026, each subject costs 144 euro with a ceiling of 720 euro a year, and the certificates stay valid for ten years, so the package can be built up and exchanged for a vwo diploma at the end. No age limit applies, which is what makes it different from every colloquium doctum above, and Dutch law lets the College voor Toetsen en Examens grant you ontheffing from individual subjects on the strength of International Baccalaureate results — the one place in Dutch education law where the IB is named. The bill is linguistic: by statute the examinations are sat in Dutch.

alternativeRouteSummary.short: No route published for this programme. Other Maastricht faculties test applicants from 21, so ask in writing.

requirements.label: Documented English proficiency
requirements.note: Maastricht resolves the English requirement through an interactive questionnaire on the programme page rather than by publishing a list, so the exact wording of the IB exemption could not be captured. It is recorded as satisfied by a full IB Diploma taught in English, which is how every other institution in this catalogue treats it, and flagged here as the one requirement on this Opportunity that rests on a pattern rather than on a quoted sentence. Confirm it on the programme page.

requirements.label: First-round review of your application documents

officialWording.text: The Board of Admissions will review your application documents and let you know by email if you have been selected for an interview.

requirements.note: A Selection Factor. Getting past it is what earns the interview; UCM publishes no scoring for it.

requirements.label: An online interview in English, 30 to 45 minutes

officialWording.text: If selected, you will be invited for an online interview in English with a UCM academic staff member. The interview takes about 30 – 45 minutes and focuses on your academic plans and how you see your education at UCM supporting these goals.

requirements.note: A Selection Factor, and the one that decides it. UCM says it is looking for "highly motivated students with a genuine passion for academics" — the interview is about what you want to study and why, not about your grades.

officialRequirementsText.text: If you have a non-Dutch diploma equivalent to the Dutch VWO diploma, you qualify - in principle - for admission to this study programme. At UCM, we are looking for highly motivated students with a genuine passion for academics. To find the right match between your academic interests and what UCM offers, we use a selective admissions process. Each year, we have 250 places available for new students.

notes: Neither national deadline applies. UCM is selective but not numerus fixus and sets its own: 1 April 2027 for an EU/EEA or Swiss applicant, 1 February 2027 for everyone else. A student who has learned '15 January or 1 May' will be wrong in both directions.
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis from 1 October 2026 against 250 places, so applying in October is not the same as applying in March even though both are inside the deadline.

University College Maastricht is absent from Maastricht's table of additional subject requirements, which means there is no subject requirement rather than that none was found. The table itself establishes the absence.

The Binding Study Advice is a real risk and belongs on the same page as the entry rules: 45 of 60 ECTS in the first year, or exclusion from UCM, Maastricht Science Programme and University College Venlo for six years.

The English requirement is the weakest claim on this record. Maastricht resolves it through an interactive questionnaire rather than a published list, so the IB exemption could not be quoted and is recorded by pattern from the other institutions here. It should be confirmed before anyone relies on it.
